doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Joe Williams and meeting him with his mother
summary: Parsons recalls his mother's love of Joe Williams and taking her to meet him at a New York club; he adds that nice people can still protect themselves, citing his martial arts.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Well I wanted to bring up a couple of people. First of all I was looking at your list of folks you’ve had associations with and my job is actually named after Joe Williams. I am the Joe Williams Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive, and he helped us get this project off the ground. Do you have memories with him?

Yeah, yes, yes. I do have memories of Joe Williams. I loved his whole style, his way of being on stage. I mean yeah he was something else. And see when I was coming up as a musician my mother always said, “You know I hope you get to –” she said her favorite singer was Joe Williams. So she was saying she would hope that maybe I would get to play with him someday, or know him or something like that. Or you know get to check him out live or something. So my mother was visiting me in New York and it happened

that Joe Williams was playing at a club there. So I said, “Hey Mom, we’re going out tonight.” And then she said, “Well where are we going?” I said, “You don’t worry about it,” you know, “just come on.” And then as we are getting ready she said, “Oh where is he playing?” She knew that that must have been why I was taking her out. So I said, “Yeah, okay you got it.” So I tipped the maître d – I guess he wouldn’t have been maître d – the waiter or the guy who met us there because – was it a restaurant? Yeah, maybe. I don’t even remember if it was just a bar. Yeah it must have been a restaurant with Joe Williams. So yeah anyway, I tipped him and said, “Look, my mother would really like to meet Joe Williams.” So I slid him a little bit of something, you know money, and then so then he went and took my mom up to meet Joe Williams there, and then the maître d came back to me and said, “Okay man, you can go back and meet him too if you want to.” So I went back and said hello. We all hung out, we had a nice little hang there.

Indeed. He was a classy guy. And he also was a good example, I’ve noticed with, I mentioned Joe Wilder, and Milt Hinton, they all had this thing that they were wonderful people, friendly. But at the same time they had so much pride in what they did, like don’t mess with that. Don’t disrespect what they do or you’ll be sorry. I mean they would react to something where they were being taken advantage of. They weren’t the kind of people that were just so nice that you could do anything and take advantage of them. They would not allow that.

Well we musn’t think that because somebody is nice that they can’t take care of themselves. In fact I think for my life I keep myself in very excellent physical condition and study martial arts since I was a teenager, and the point is to lead a gentle life, to be a nice person, to not have to be mean to people or to be like this or any of that kind of stuff. Be nice and loving. To not have to descend to somebody else’s level if they want to insult me or something like that. You know to be above all of these things.
